reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 22 rows and 5 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 3 rows and 11 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 15 rows and 18 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 10 rows and 15 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 4 rows and 14 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The stem says 'Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all', but the key demands the exact product and every distractor sits within two of it (seed 42 keys 110 against 109, 111 and 112). A genuine estimate cannot discriminate those options, so the item covertly grades exact multiplication. The verb 'Illustrate' is never exercised - no tile diagram, drawing or partially covered figure appears.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency covers 'a square or rectangle', yet all five seeds use unequal dimensions - 22 by 5, 3 by 11, 15 by 18, 10 by 15 and 4 by 14. The square sub-case, where rows equal columns, is never generated in the sample.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 44's '15 rows and 18 columns' needs two-digit by two-digit multiplication and seed 42's '22 rows and 5 columns' needs two-digit by one-digit, both beyond Grade 3 Quarter 1 where multiplication is only being introduced. Counting or estimating 270 individual tiles is likewise not a Q1 task.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: A single frozen sentence frame is reused at every seed with only the two dimensions changing. There is no inverse variant giving the tile count and one side, no partially tiled rectangle to complete, and no labelling of the tile unit in square centimetres or metres.

competency_alignment.rationale: Areas run 33, 56, 110, 150 and 270 with no ordering by difficulty, and because the distractors are always off-by-one neighbours of the key, the practice trains exact product recall rather than the tiling-and-estimating reasoning the competency names.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Hand-checking confirms all five keys are arithmetically correct (22x5=110, 3x11=33, 15x18=270, 10x15=150, 4x14=56), but a 15 by 18 array yielding 270 tiles far exceeds what a Grade 3 Quarter 1 pupil can tile, count or estimate; dimensions should stay near 10 by 10 or below.
